newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up on selective share gains.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up on selective share gains.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index rose on Monday on marginal price gains in a few selected shares, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index rose 7.54 points to stand at 3051.68. Turnover was posted at 5.120 million shillings on 152,061 shares compared to 74.244 million shillings on 1,590,431 shares on Friday.
Bourse officials said traded volume was down compared to Friday because of a lack of block trades.

A senior broker said prices for some shares rose on a lot of buying, with high demand compared to limited supply. Kenya Commercial Bank and Standard Chartered Bank shares met good demand and subsequently rose.
Kenya Commercial Bank rose to 54 from 52.50 on 10,200 shares, Standard Chartered Bank traded 49,027 shares at 45 from 44 and National Bank of Kenya rose to 15.80 from 15.70.

"There is a lot of interest in the Standard Chartered Bank share as investors believe that the current market price is undervalued," one dealer said. "This interest will also probably continue for some time."

Brokers explained the surge in the Kenya Commercial Bank share price as caused by a rush to purchase the already limited stock on offer. A primary offer in the bank will close on October 15, reducing government ownership by a further 10 percent to 60 percent, according to offer documents.

Kenya Airways traded 25,246 shares at 9.85 from 9.90 on investor pressure to sell. The airline had eased to way below its June flotation price of 11.25 shillings, mainly on disputes between management and pilots that undermined profits.
Brokers said a threat by Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni to cut power supply to Kenya appeared to undermine the power stock. Kenya Power & Lighting Company fell 3.0 shillings to 113.
